newsitem.title: USA: Former Ford Models executive sues.
newsitem.headline: Former Ford Models executive sues.

text.p: A former top executive at Ford Models Inc. has sued for a court order to allow her to inspect the famed model agency's financial records for "corporate waste," according to court documents released Tuesday.

In her lawsuit, former Ford Co-President Marion Smith said she was seeking to determine "the full extent of the corporate waste ... (and) the improper expenditure of corporate funds for unjustified personal perquisites."
The lawsuit was filed Friday in Delaware Chancery Court but not released until Tuesday. No court dates have been set.

Smith, who worked for Ford Models for 27 years, alleged that Ford Models' founding family members used company funds for rent, "the salaries of nannies, personal chauffeurs and other household staff."

According to court papers, Smith owns 1,000 shares in Ford representing 16 percent of the privately held company's stock, which she bought at a discount in 1987 with a $30,000 loan from agency co-founder Gerard Ford.

But in July, Ford attorney Maury Josephson of the firm Skadden Arps alleged in a letter to Smith's attorney that Smith had forfeited her stock ownership because of an unspecified "serious breach of her employment agreement" and that her request to see the company's financial records was an attempt to obtain "an exorbitant settlement" from Ford.

Smith was paid $200,000 a year to head the women's division of New York-based Ford, which over decades launched such models as Lauren Hutton, Jean Shrimpton and Christy Turlington. The other co-president, Joey Hunter, headed the men's division.
Smith resigned in September 1995 to join rival agency Company Management, taking with her several models, including supermodels Jerry Hall and Rachel Hunter.

Smith's attorney, Jeffrey Rosenberg, said in an interview that the dispute began when Katie Ford, daughter of founders Eileen and Gerard Ford, took charge of the agency and allegedly sought to take away power from "all the people who had loyalty to her parents."
Competing lawsuits related to the employment agreement were filed by Smith and the Ford agency in New York last year and are pending.
Josephson said he would not comment on the latest lawsuit. Calls to Katie Ford's office were referred to a spokesman who did not respond to a request for comment.
Ford Models spokesman Andrew Freedman declined to comment on the lawsuit.
In addition to New York, the agency has other offices in the United States, France, Canada, Argentina and Brazil.
